priceSnapshot.note: Spot is 63,534.2 against endday's 62,797.3 - UP 736.9 points, +1.17%, in six and a half unattended hours. The 24h window on the same tick reads open 63,050.2, high 63,720.0, low 62,715.7, so the entire overnight range sits above the 62,521.8 flush low and the low of the window never reached endday's resting stop at 62,680.0, missing it by 35.7 points. reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $62,840.0 - the low of the post-snapshot session, printed on the 00:45Z 15m bar. The line moves UP 124.3 points from endday's 62,715.7, and it moves up because the structure it was protecting has been rebuilt: price has reclaimed the 1H ema20 (63,265.4), ema50 (63,179.3) and ema100 (63,287.1) and held above all three for five consecutive settled bars. A settled close back under 62,840.0 would undo that reclaim in one move and re-open the single largest object on the map, the 62,623.1 liquidation band carrying 910.85K of leverage against a window maximum of 918.34K.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 4H close above $63,970.0 - just through the 4H ema200 at 63,965.1. That level is chosen because it is the first gate that clears three overhead obstacles at once: the daily ema20 at 63,816.3, the 63,824.4 liquidation band carrying 192.56K, and the 4H ema100 at 63,798.5. Everything between 63,798 and 63,965 is one wall and half-measures inside it are noise. The confirmation that would matter beyond price is open interest CONTINUING to fall through the break - this bounce has been built on OI dropping 1.45%, which is shorts covering, and a break that finally runs on RISING OI would be the first evidence in four sessions that a buyer rather than a coverer is doing the work.

decisionBox.changed: The stance inverts back from REDUCE to ADD after one session. Endday published a reduce line at 62,715.7 and an add gate at 63,090.5 and was explicit that the gate would need falling open interest to be believed; both halves of that test resolved in the bull's favour overnight - the gate fired on the 02:00Z settled bar and open interest fell 1.45% through the move - so the desk is following its own published rule rather than its prior direction. The reduce line rises 124.3 points to 62,840.0, the add gate rises 879.5 points to 63,970.0 because the near reclaim has already happened and the next decision is a wall not a step, invalidation holds unchanged at 62,521.8, and the stopOrder flag drops back to NOT recommended because the wallet carries no futures, the next report is roughly four and a half hours away rather than six and a half, and spot sits 694.2 points above the reduce line rather than 81.6.

liquidation.note: 192.56K on the CoinGlass Model-3 leverage scale, whose maximum this window is 918.34K. It is the nearest resting fuel overhead and it sits 8.1 points ABOVE the daily ema20 at 63,816.3, so band and moving average form a single wall rather than two tests.
79.42K - thin. Between 63,824 and 64,559 the map is close to empty, which is the argument for why a clean break of the 63,798-63,965 wall could travel further than the immediate levels suggest.

910.85K against a window maximum of 918.34K - 99.2% of the brightest band on the entire 48-hour map and by a wide margin the largest single concentration in either direction. It sits 911.1 points under spot and 92.6 points under the 24h low, and it is the reason the pull stays DOWN even after an 800-point bounce: the bounce has moved price away from the magnet without removing it.
99.81K - the next shelf beneath the magnet, only relevant if 62,623.1 is taken out. Its size relative to the band above it says the 62,623 level is where the fuel is concentrated, not spread.

liquidityMagnet.source: CoinGlass Liquidation Heatmap Model 3 (Binance BTC/USDT Perpetual, 48 hour, liquidity threshold 0.9), read via browser hover tooltips - the OKX realized-liquidation feed was discarded on the freshness guard
liquidityMagnet.note: The asymmetry is the whole reading: 910.85K below against 192.56K above is 4.73 to 1 in favour of the downside magnet. That does not make the bounce fake, but it does mean the market has an unresolved object underneath it, and every hour price spends between 63,500 and 63,800 without breaking the wall is an hour the magnet keeps its claim. Distance cuts the other way - spot is now 911 points above the band where six hours ago it was 174 - so the pull is real but no longer imminent.

liquidations.note: THE HEADLINE IS THAT LEVERAGE CAME OUT ON THE WAY UP. OKX BTC-USDT-SWAP open interest is $2,091,561,886 read live in-browser at 07:17:55Z against endday's $2,122,316,880 - DOWN $30,754,994 or 1.45% - while price ROSE 736.9 points. That is the exact inverse of endday's configuration, where OI rose 0.34% into a 367.8-point fall, and it is the signature endday itself named in its addIf text as the confirmation that would matter: shorts covering rather than longs being tempted back in. The OKX long/short account ratio agrees, at 2.03 on the 06:00Z print against 2.24 at endday and a 2.28 peak at 22:00Z - retail long crowding has unwound by 0.25 in six hours. Funding on the same swap is +0.00375% into the 16:00Z settlement against +0.01000% at endday, so the carry cost of being long has been cut by roughly 62%. All three positioning measures moved the same way and all three moved in the bulls' favour. The realized-liquidation feed is DISCARDED and longsUsd/shortsUsd are null: OKX's public liquidation-orders endpoint returned a newest fill stamped 08:27Z on 16 AUGUST at 63,030-63,103, over twenty-one hours old and 431-504 points away from spot, which fails this desk's freshness guard outright. The CoinGlass header carried a 24h liquidation total of $129,855,297, +203.36%, but that figure is market-wide across all assets and carries no BTC long/short split, so it is recorded here as context and not as a BTC number. CoinGlass's own 24h long/short reads 53.14%/46.86%, a much flatter 1.13 ratio on a different and broader account base than OKX's 2.03.

calibration.note: The prior report is yesterday's 2026-08-16-endday, published at 19:45:00-05:00 with spot at 62,797.3. Its reduce line at 62,715.7 did NOT fire - the lowest settled 1H close in the window was 62,903.9 on the 00:00Z bar, 188.2 points clear, and the window low of 62,715.7 tagged the level to the tick without a settled close through it. Its add gate at 63,090.5 DID fire, on the 02:00Z bar at 63,104.6, and held: the five bars since settled 63,407.1, 63,426.9, 63,542.0, 63,516.0 and 63,663.4. Its resting stop at 62,680.0 was never reached, surviving by 35.7 points. actingHelped is FALSE. Endday's decision was to sell a fifth of the spot book at 62,797.3 into what it called a defensive trim ahead of the overnight gap; spot marks 736.9 points higher at 63,534.2, so that trim cost roughly 0.38 USDT of opportunity on 0.00051647 BTC - the largest miss in the file, ahead of midday's 0.070 USDT. Three things are worth recording precisely. FIRST, endday's central positioning argument was falsifiable and has been falsified within six hours: it wrote that open interest rising 0.34% through a cascade meant the burned long cohort had been replaced at a worse price and that this configuration produces a second leg rather than a bottom. Open interest instead fell 1.45%, the long/short ratio fell from 2.24 to 2.03, funding fell from +0.01000% to +0.00375%, and no second leg came. The observation of the moment was accurate; the extrapolation from it was wrong. SECOND, and to endday's real credit, it wrote its own escape hatch into the addIf text - that the confirmation which would matter is open interest FALLING through a reclaim, because that would say shorts are covering. That is exactly what happened, and it happened at exactly the level endday nominated. A report that names the condition under which it would be wrong, and then is wrong under that condition, has done its job even though the trade lost. THIRD, this is the mirror image of the failure logged the previous three sessions. From 14 to 16 August the recurring fault was arguing against an ADD and taking it anyway at reduced size; tonight the fault is the opposite - arguing for a REDUCE on a trigger that had genuinely fired, and executing it correctly, only for the trigger itself to be the wrong rule for a post-cascade tape. Publishing a reduce level under a liquidation flush and then obeying it sells the bottom of the flush. That is a new and specific lesson: after a cascade has already run, a reduce line placed at the flush low is not protection, it is a stop-loss sitting exactly where the liquidity is.
